nodes.name: Fast rate bounds
nodes.statement: Fast rate bounds hold for near orthogonal designs and bound the prediction error in terms of the sparsity of the regression vectors.
differentia: bound the prediction error in terms of the sparsity of the regression vectors

nodes.name: Slow rate bounds
nodes.statement: Slow rate bounds, on the other hand, hold for any design and bound the prediction error in terms of the penalty value of the regression vectors.
differentia: bound the prediction error in terms of the penalty value of the regression vectors

nodes.name: Penalty bounds and sparsity bounds
nodes.statement: To avoid confusion in the following, we will use the terms \emph{penalty bounds}  instead of slow rate bounds  and \emph{sparsity bounds} instead of fast rate bounds.
nodes.statement_short: Renames slow rate bounds as penalty bounds and fast rate bounds as sparsity bounds.

nodes.name: Linear regression model
nodes.statement_short: Linear model $Y=X\beta^*+\varepsilon$ with outcome, design matrix, regression vector and noise.

nodes.name: Linear regression model equation
nodes.statement: \textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}= \textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\beta^*}} +\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}
nodes.label: eq:model

nodes.name: Penalized estimator with link function
nodes.statement_short: Estimators minimizing a link function of the squared residual norm plus a penalty with tuning parameter $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Composite-norm penalized estimator
nodes.statement_short: The estimator class: link of squared residuals plus a weighted sum of $\ell_{q_j}$-norms of $M_j\beta$.

nodes.name: Estimator criterion (2)
nodes.statement: \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat \beta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}} \in \mathop{\mathrm{arg\,min}}_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p}\big\{\ensuremath{g}\big(\,\normtwo{\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\beta}^2\big)+\sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}\ensuremath{\lambda}_j\,\normqj{\ensuremath{M}_j\beta}\big\}\,.
nodes.label: eq:estimator

nodes.name: Link function assumptions
nodes.statement: The link function~$\ensuremath{g}:\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\ensuremath{g}(0)=0,$ is continuous and strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, and  is continuously differentiable on~$(0,\infty)$ with strictly positive and non-increasing derivative $\ensuremath{g}'(x):=\frac{d}{dy}\ensuremath{g}(y)\big\lvert_{y=x}.
nodes.statement_short: $g$ vanishes at 0, is continuous, strictly increasing, and $C^1$ on $(0,\infty)$ with positive non-increasing derivative $g'$.

nodes.name: Strict convexity of the link composition
nodes.statement: Moreover, the function $\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty):$ $\alpha\mapsto g(\,\normtwo{\alpha}^2)$ is assumed to be strictly convex.

nodes.name: Positive tuning parameters
nodes.statement: First, we assume that the tuning parameter $\ensuremath{\lambda}:=(\ensuremath{\lambda}_1,\dots,\ensuremath{\lambda}_k)^\top$ is in $(0,\infty)^k.$

nodes.name: Trivial joint kernel of the penalty matrices
nodes.statement: We then assume that the matrices $\ensuremath{M}_1,\dots,\ensuremath{M}_{\ensuremath{k}}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}$ satisfy $\bigcap_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}} \operatorname{Ker}(\ensuremath{M}_j)=\{\mathbf 0_{p\times p}\},$ where $\operatorname{Ker}$ denotes the kernel of a matrix.
nodes.statement_short: The penalty matrices $M_1,\dots,M_k$ have trivial common kernel.

nodes.name: $\ell_{q_j}$ penalty norms
nodes.statement: Finally, the single norms $\normqj{\cdot}$ with $q_j\geq 1$ are the regular $\ell_{q_j}$-norms on~$\mathbb{R}^{p}.$

nodes.name: Dual norms
nodes.statement:
Their dual norms are denoted by~$
ormqjd{\cdot}$, and it holds that $
ormqjd{\cdot}=
ormpj{\cdot}$ for $p_j\in[1,\infty]$ such that ${1}/{p_j} + {1}/{q_j} =1.$

nodes.name: The penalty is a norm
nodes.statement: Since each $\normqj{\cdot}$ is a norm, and since the rows of the matrices $\ensuremath{M_j}$ span the entire~$\mathbb{R}^p$, the penalty is indeed a norm.
assumptions: the rows of the matrices $\ensuremath{M_j}$ span the entire~$\mathbb{R}^p$
conclusions: the penalty is indeed a norm

nodes.name: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse
nodes.statement: For this, we first denote by $A^+$ the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of a matrix $A$.

nodes.name: Projection matrices $P_j$
nodes.statement_short: Projection matrices $P_j$ with $\sum_j P_j M_j^+ M_j = I$, which exist by the rank assumption.

nodes.name: Partition of identity (3)
nodes.statement: \sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}\textcolor{black}{P_j}\ensuremath{M_j}^{+}\ensuremath{M_j}=\operatorname{I}_{p\times p}\,.
nodes.label: eq:partition

nodes.name: Noise assumption
nodes.statement: More specifically, we assume that $\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}\neq \bold{0}_n$ and $\min_{j\in\{1,\dots,\ensuremath{k}\}}\norm{(\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} P_j\ensuremath{M}_j^{+})^\top\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}_{q_j}^*>0$ with probability one.
nodes.statement_short: Almost surely $Y\neq 0$ and every dual norm $\|(XP_jM_j^+)^\top\varepsilon\|_{q_j}^*$ is positive.

nodes.name: Lower bound for lasso prediction rates
nodes.statement: Indeed, it has been shown that the rates for lasso prediction \cite[Proposition~4]{ArnakMoYo14} (even when the noise is Gaussian) can not be improved in general beyond $1/\sqrt n$, which corresponds to our bound up to log-factors --- see the Examples section.
conclusions: the rates for lasso prediction \cite[Proposition~4]{ArnakMoYo14} (even when the noise is Gaussian) can not be improved in general beyond $1/\sqrt n$
also_stated_at: Importantly, the rate is lower bounded by $1/\sqrt n$ --- unless further assumptions on the design matrix~\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ are imposed~\cite[Proposition~4]{ArnakMoYo14}.

nodes.name: Fast rate for lasso under RE-type assumptions
nodes.statement: Under RE-type assumptions~\cite{Sara09}, one can find the rate ${s\log p}/{n}$ for the lasso prediction error, where $s$ is the number of non-zero elements in $\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\beta^*}}$.
conclusions: one can find the rate ${s\log p}/{n}$ for the lasso prediction error

nodes.name: Optimality of l1 rates in out-of-sample prediction
nodes.statement: On the other hand, the optimality of the $\ell_1$-related rates suggested in~\cite{Greenshtein04} and the applicability of the results to other estimators considered in our paper remain open questions.

nodes.statement: We first consider a tuning parameter $\overline{\lambda}\in (0,\infty)^{\ensuremath{k}}$  that satisfies the equality in Lemma~\ref{re:existence} with $\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_1,\dots,\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_{\ensuremath{k}}=1$.

nodes.name: Estimator $\overline\beta$
nodes.statement: We set $\overline \beta:=\widehat\beta^{\overline{\lambda}}$ for ease of notation.

nodes.name: Oracle inequality with u=0.5 (4)
nodes.statement:
rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-\overline  eta)}^2\le\min_{\substack{	extcolor{black}{ eta}\in\mathbb{R}^p}} \Big\{ rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-	extcolor{black}{ eta})}^2+ rac{4}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}\,  
ormqjd{(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  P_j\ensuremath{M}_j^{+})^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}  \,

nodes.statement:
To bring this on a more abstract level, we denote the prediction loss by $	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{L}}(	extcolor{black}{ eta}):=\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-	extcolor{black}{ eta})}^2/n$ and introduce model classes $\ensuremath{\mathcal F_{	extcolor{black}{v}}}:=\{	extcolor{black}{ eta}\in\mathbb{R}^p:4\sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}\,  
ormqjd{(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  P_j\ensuremath{M}_j^{+})^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}  \, 
ormqj{\ensuremath{M}_j 	extcolor{black}{ eta}}/n=	extcolor{black}{v}\}$ indexed by~$	extcolor{black}{v}\in[0,\infty).$

nodes.name: Penalized loss $L_{\bf a}$
nodes.statement_short: Loss combining in-sample prediction error and weighted penalty $\sum_j a_j\|M_j\beta\|_{q_j}/n$.

nodes.name: Oracle inequality for the penalized loss
nodes.statement_short: With $a_j=2(c_j-1)\|\cdot\|^*$, the estimator's $L_{\bf a}$ loss is within a constant factor of the minimal $L_{\bf a}$ loss.

nodes.statement:
rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-\overline  eta)}^2\le rac{2}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}\,  
ormqjd{(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  P_j\ensuremath{M}_j^{+})^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}  \, 
ormqj{\ensuremath{M}_j  eta^*}\,.

nodes.name: Optimality of the tuning parameter lambda-bar for the bound
nodes.statement: The tuning parameter $\overline{\lambda}$ minimizes  $\sum_{j=1}^{\ensuremath{k}}(1+\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_j)\,  \normqjd{(\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  P_j\ensuremath{M}_j^{+})^\top\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}  \, \normqj{\ensuremath{M}_j \textcolor{black}{\beta}}/(n(1-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{u}})),$ the first term on the right-hand side of the bound, as a function of $\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_1,\dots,\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_{\ensuremath{k}}$ under the constraint that $\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_1,\dots,\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{c}}_{\ensuremath{k}}\geq 1$ (which implies that the  terms on the right-hand side that depend on the estimator can be dropped).
nodes.statement_short: $\overline\lambda$ minimizes the penalty term of the bound over $c_j\ge 1$.

nodes.name: Tuning parameters minimizing the prediction loss
nodes.statement: Explicit formulations of tuning parameters that minimize the prediction loss are to date unknown.

nodes.name: Five properties of the penalty bound
nodes.statement: We conclude this section highlighting five other properties of Theorem~\ref{r:finalbound} (much of this becomes more lucid in the context of the specific examples discussed in the next section): First, the bound involves the values of the tuning parameters to the power one and holds for any design matrix~\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}. The bound contains the penalty values of the regression vectors. Hence, the bounds are penalty bounds. Second, the oracle inequality holds for any distribution of the noise~\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}. Third, the bounds hold for any sample size $n$; in particular, the bounds are non-asymptotic. Fourth, the bounds become smaller if the correlations in~$\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}$ become larger, cf.~\cite{Hebiri13}. Fifth, the link function~$\ensuremath{g}$ appears in the existence result on tuning parameters but not in the prediction bound. This last, interesting point clarifies the role of the link function: its essential purpose is to ``reshuffle'' the tuning parameter path. One can relate this observation to the discussion of the lasso/square-root lasso below.
nodes.statement_short: The bound is a penalty bound for any design, any noise, any $n$, improves with correlations, and does not involve the link function.

nodes.name: Lasso
Derivation of the standard lasso penalty bound
nodes.statement:
The proofs use that lasso objective function is minimal at~\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}, that is, for any $	extcolor{black}{ eta}\in\mathbb{R}^p,$ it holds that
 egin{equation*}
  
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}\leq 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}\,.
\end{equation*}
This is equivalent to 
 egin{equation*}
  
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*+	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}\leq 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*+	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}
\end{equation*}
and
 egin{multline*}
  
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*}^2+2\langle	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*,	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}angle+
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}\
\leq 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*}^2+2\langle	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*,	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}angle+
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}^2+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}\,.
\end{multline*}
Invoking the model~\eqref{eq:model} and consolidating, this yields
 egin{equation*}
    
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{ eta^*}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2\leq 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}^2+2\inprod{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}-\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}\,.
\end{equation*}
H"older's inequality and the triangle inequality then lead to
 egin{equation*}
    
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{ eta^*}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2\leq 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} eta^*-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}	extcolor{black}{ eta}}^2+2\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}(\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}+
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}})+\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}-\ensuremath{\lambda}\,
ormone{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}\,.
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Basic inequality from minimality of the lasso objective, then the model, H\"older and triangle inequalities.

nodes.name: Standard lasso penalty bound
nodes.statement:
Hence, for $\lambda=\overline{\lambda}=2\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}},$ we eventually find
 egin{equation*}
    rac{1}{n}\, 
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{ eta^*}}-\overline  eta)}^2\leq\min_{	extcolor{black}{ eta}\in\mathbb{R}^p}\Big\{\,  rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-	extcolor{black}{ eta})}^2+ rac{4}{n}\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}\,
ormone{	extcolor{black}{ eta}}\Big\}\,.
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: For $\lambda=2\|X^\top\varepsilon\|_\infty$ the lasso prediction error is at most $\min_\beta$ of approximation error plus $4\|X^\top\varepsilon\|_\infty\|\beta\|_1/n$.

nodes.name: Inequality (4) recovers the lasso bound
nodes.statement: Observing that $\ensuremath{k}=1$ and $\ensuremath{M}_1=P_1=\operatorname{I}_{p\times p}$ in this example, one can check that \eqref{special1} recovers this bound.

nodes.name: Improved lasso bound from (5)
nodes.statement_short: With $\beta=\beta^*$, (5) gives the lasso bound $2\|X^\top\varepsilon\|_\infty\|\beta^*\|_1/n$, a factor 2 better.

nodes.name: Lasso rates under Gaussian noise
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian noise, normalized design: $\overline\lambda\approx\sigma\sqrt{n\log p}$ and error $\lesssim\sigma\sqrt{\log p/n}\|\beta^*\|_1$.

nodes.name: Lasso with tailored tuning parameters
nodes.statement: We finally note that one can also include ``tailored'' tuning parameters, which corresponds to considering the lasso as a specification of our general framework with $\ensuremath{k}=p$ and not necessarily equal tuning parameters $\ensuremath{\lambda}_1,\dots,\ensuremath{\lambda}_p.$ One can check easily that in particular if $(\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^\top\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}})_1,\dots,(\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^\top\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}})_p$ i.i.d, one obtains the same bounds as above.

nodes.name: Square-root lasso
Square-root lasso penalty bound
nodes.statement:
In our framework, $\ensuremath{k}=1$ and $\ensuremath{M}_1=P_1=\operatorname{I}_{p	imes p},$ so that $\overline{\lambda}=\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}/\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\overline{\lambda}}}$ and the prediction bound~\eqref{special2} reads
 egin{equation*}
 rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-\overline  eta)}^2 \le  rac 2 n\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  ^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}\,   
ormone{ eta^*}\,.
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: For the square-root lasso, $\overline\lambda=\|X^\top\varepsilon\|_\infty/\|Y-X\hat\beta\|_2$ and (5) gives the lasso-type bound.

nodes.name: Square-root lasso tuning parameter is independent of sigma
nodes.statement:
For example,  if $	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}_1,\dots,	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}_n\stackrel{\mathclap{
ormalfont\mbox{\scriptsize iid}}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ and $(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}})_{jj}=n$ for all~$j\in\{1,\dots,p\}$, it holds ootnote{see Page~\pageref{sqrtexproof} for some hints} that $\overline{\lambda}\approx 
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}/\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}\approx\sqrt{\log(p)}$, which is independent of $\sigma.$
nodes.statement_short: Under Gaussian noise and normalized design, the square-root lasso $\overline\lambda\approx\sqrt{\log p}$, free of $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Slope estimator
nodes.statement_short: Least squares with sorted-$\ell_1$ penalty $\lambda\sum_j\omega_j|\beta|_{(j)}$, non-increasing weights.

nodes.name: Slope estimator penalty bound
nodes.statement:
A promising case for the slope estimator is the one where $	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}_1,\dots,	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}_n\stackrel{\mathclap{
ormalfont\mbox{\scriptsize iid}}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2) $ and $(	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}})_{jj}=n$ for all~$j\in\{1,\dots,p\}.$ The weights can then be chosen as $\omega_j:=2\sigma\sqrt{n\log(2p/j)}$ in the spirit of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure~\cite{Bogdan15,Su16}, and  a theoretically justified choice of the tuning parameter is $\lambda>4+\sqrt 2$~\cite[Equation~(2.5)]{Bellec16}. In particular, this choice works in the sense of the first part of  Theorem~ef{r:finalbound}, and one finds the bound  $\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-\overline  eta)}^2/n \lesssim \ensuremath{\lambda} \sigma\sqrt{\log(p)/n}\ 
ormone{ eta^*}$, for example, which coincides with the bounds above.
nodes.statement_short: With BH-type weights and $\lambda>4+\sqrt2$, slope satisfies the theorem and has the lasso-type rate.

nodes.name: Elastic net
Elastic net penalty bound
nodes.statement:
This is not directly in the form~\eqref{eq:estimator}. However, one can use the usual trick writing the estimator as a lasso with augmented data, cf.~\cite[Lemma~1]{Hebiri11}. Using $\ensuremath{M}_1=P_1=\operatorname{I}_{p	imes p}$, our results then hold for any  tuning parameters that satisfy $\ensuremath{\lambda}_1=2\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}-\ensuremath{\lambda}_2 eta^*}$. For example, we can set $\overline{\lambda}_2=\mathop{\mathrm{arg\,min}}_{\ensuremath{\lambda}_2}
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}-\ensuremath{\lambda}_2 eta^*}$ and $\overline{\lambda}_1=2\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}-\overline{\lambda}_2 eta^*}$. The bound in~\eqref{special2}, for example, then reads
 egin{equation*}
 rac{1}{n}\,
ormtwo{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}( eta^*-\overline  eta)}^2\le  rac{2}{n}\, 
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}-\overline{\lambda}_2 eta^*}\,
ormone{ eta^*} \le  rac{2}{n}\,
ormsup{	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}  ^	op	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}}\,   
ormone{ eta^*}\,.
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Writing the elastic net as an augmented-data lasso, (5) gives a bound no worse than the lasso's.

nodes.name: Group lasso with non-overlapping groups
nodes.statement_short: Non-overlapping group lasso: $\overline\lambda=2\max_l\|(X^\top\varepsilon)_{G_l}\|_2$ and (5) gives a group-norm bound.

nodes.name: Trend filtering
nodes.statement_short: Penalized fit with $\ell_1$ penalty on $l$-fold discrete differences $M=D^l$.

Total variation / fused lasso penalty bound
nodes.statement_short: For $l=1$ (total variation/fused lasso), explicit $D^+$ gives $\overline\lambda=2\|D^{+\top}\varepsilon\|_\infty$ and the bound.

nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|Y-X\overline\beta\|_2$ above and below by $\sqrt n$ up to lower order via the triangle inequality and maximal inequalities.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of fitted values and convexity of the solution set
nodes.statement_short: All minimizers have the same fitted values $X\hat\beta$ and the set of minimizers is convex.

nodes.name: Continuity in the tuning parameter
assumptions: Let $\mathbb{R}^{\ensuremath{k}}$ be  equipped with the Euclidean norm, and $\mathbb{R}$ be equipped with the  absolute value norm.
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda\mapsto g(\|Y-X\hat\beta^\lambda\|^2)$ and $\lambda\mapsto\|Y-X\hat\beta^\lambda\|^2$ are continuous on $(0,\infty)^k$.

nodes.statement: With probability one, it holds that $\,\normtwo{\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat \beta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2>0$ and $g'(\,\normtwo{\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat \beta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2)> 0$ for any tuning parameter $\lambda\in(0,\infty)^{\ensuremath{k}}$.
conclusions: With probability one, it holds that $\,\normtwo{\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat \beta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2>0$ and $g'(\,\normtwo{\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-\textcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat \beta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}}^2)> 0$ for any tuning parameter $\lambda\in(0,\infty)^{\ensuremath{k}}$.

Using this with $a=	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}} \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\widehat  eta}^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}}$ and $	ilde a= 	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{Y}}-	extcolor{black}{\ensuremath{X}}\ensuremath{	ilde eta^{\ensuremath{\lambda}}},$ and invoking the convexity of the norms~$
